title: Oligo(dT) Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization for Poly(A) mRNAs in Drosophila Tissues
author: Ankur Kumar

Note: PFA is a polymer with a wide range of monomeric and oligomeric units of formaldehyde. It dissolves in water and depolymerizes into a monomeric form of formaldehyde. Formaldehyde can crosslink cellular constituents, particularly proteins with lysine residues. Formaldehyde is a toxic chemical; therefore, always wear a mask and gloves during handling.
Note: DEPC irreversibly inactivates RNase contamination that may be present in dH 2 O. It is carcinogenic and, therefore, needs to be handled carefully.
Note: Yeast tRNA is used as a nonspecific blocking agent, protecting both the probe and cellular RNA.

Dextran sulfate (Merck, catalog number: 265152-M) Note: Dextran sulfate is a highly hydrated polysaccharide that acts as an effective volume exclusion agent. It affects the probe concentration by preventing its solubilization in water and thus gives higher hybridization rates in aqueous solutions.

Note: RNase inhibitors directly bind with RNases in a non-competitive mode and thus block their activity. They have been widely used to stop the activity of RNases that are present within the cell. The presence of 1 U/μL RNase inhibitor can block most of the RNase activity during FISH.

Note: Formamide interferes with hydrogen bonding in double-stranded polynucleotides and thus destabilizes double-strand formation. The presence of formamide in hybridization buffer, therefore, reduces the melting and annealing temperature, which keeps the tissue morphology relatively intact due to low incubation temperature. The working concentration of formamide in hybridization buffer varies from 10% to 50%, depending upon the probe length and its GC content.

Note: DAPI is a fluorescent stain that binds to the AT-rich region of DNA, with excitation at 405 nm and emission spectrum between 420 and 480 nm (blue color). The fluorescence of DAPI is enhanced several times following its binding with DNA.

ProLong TM Gold antifade mountant (Thermo, catalog number: P10114 ) Note: ProLong TM Gold antifade mountant is a commercially available glycerol-based mounting media supplemented with an antifading agent that protects the fluorescent signal intensity.

Riboprobe; probes used here for FISH are single-stranded, non-self-complementary short stretches of polynucleotides (20–1500 nucleotide long DNA or RNA) that have a complementary sequence to the target RNA. In the present study, we used RNase Free HPLC Purified 45 nucleotide long stretch of oligo(dT) probe tagged with Cy3 at the 5′ end. We customized the probe and procured it from Integrated DNA Technologies (IDT) Solutions

steps.title: Gather reagents and supplies
steps.instruction: Collect all chemicals, reagents, and equipment listed, including catalog numbers: Ether (SRL 25049), NaCl (Himedia MB023), KCl (Himedia TC010), Na₂HPO₄ (Himedia GRM168), KH₂PO₄ (Himedia GRM1188), Sodium citrate (Himedia TC526U), NP‑40 (Thermo 85124), Triton X‑100 (Himedia MB031), DAPI (Thermo 62247), PFA (Himedia RM3660), DEPC (Himedia MB076), yeast tRNA (Thermo AM7119), dextran sulfate (Merck 265152‑M), RNase inhibitor (Thermo EO0382), Formamide (Sigma 15706), ProLong Gold antifade (Thermo P10114), Cy3‑labeled 45‑nt oligo(dT) probe (IDT), glass slides, coverslips, fine forceps, dissecting needles, nail polish, dark chamber, etherizer, microcentrifuge tubes, rotator, pipettes, and a 500 µL tube.

steps.title: Prepare 10× PBS
steps.instruction: Dissolve 80 g NaCl, 2 g KCl, 14.4 g Na₂HPO₄, and 2.45 g KH₂PO₄ in 800 mL dH₂O, adjust pH to 7.4, bring volume to 1 L, autoclave, store at room temperature. Dilute 1:9 with dH₂O to obtain 1× PBS and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 20× SSC
steps.instruction: Dissolve 175.3 g NaCl and 77.4 g sodium citrate in 800 mL dH₂O, adjust pH to 7.0 with HCl, bring volume to 1 L, autoclave, store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 4% PFA
steps.instruction: Dissolve 4.0 g PFA in 75 mL 1× PBS at 60 °C with stirring for 10 min, add 5 N NaOH dropwise until solution clears, filter, adjust pH to 7.0 with HCl or NaOH, bring volume to 100 mL with 1× PBS, aliquot and store at –20 °C. Defrost an aliquot and use the same day; preferably prepare fresh small volumes as needed.

steps.title: Prepare 50% dextran sulfate
steps.instruction: Slowly dissolve 20 g dextran sulfate powder in 30 mL DEPC‑treated dH₂O, rotate overnight, bring volume to 40 mL with dH₂O, aliquot and store at –20 °C. Handle viscous solution with care.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1% DEPC solution
steps.instruction: Mix 0.1 mL DEPC with 100 mL dH₂O, incubate 4 h at 37 °C, then autoclave. Use DEPC‑treated dH₂O for all RNase‑free buffers.

steps.title: Prepare 0.3% PBST
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.03 mL Triton X‑100 in 10 mL 1× PBS to obtain 0.3% PBST; use as washing buffer.

steps.title: Prepare 100 mg/mL yeast tRNA stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 25 mg yeast tRNA powder in 250 µL DEPC‑treated dH₂O, aliquot and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 1 µg/mL DAPI working solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 mg DAPI in 1 mL dH₂O (stock 1 mg/mL), store at –20 °C; dilute 1:1000 in 1× PBS to obtain 1 µg/mL working solution, store at 4 °C for weeks.

steps.title: Make permeabilization buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 1 µL Triton X‑100, 1 µL NP‑40, 2.5 µL 40 U/µL RNase inhibitor, and 95.5 µL 1× PBS (total 100 µL); use fresh.

steps.title: Make hybridization buffer
steps.instruction: In 39 µL DEPC‑treated dH₂O add 25 µL formamide, 10 µL 20× SSC (pH 7.0), 20 µL 50% dextran sulfate, 1 µL 100 mg/mL yeast tRNA, and 5 µL 100 ng/µL Cy3‑labeled oligo(dT) riboprobe (final 100 µL). Use fresh.

steps.title: Make wash buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 25 µL formamide, 10 µL 20× SSC, and 65 µL DEPC‑treated dH₂O (total 100 µL); use fresh.

steps.title: Collect and anesthetize larvae
steps.instruction: Set up desired cross in standard cornmeal food, collect actively wandering third‑instar larvae of the Nup107GFP/Nup107GFP genotype, and anesthetize with ether in an etherizer.

steps.title: Wash and dry larvae
steps.instruction: Rinse larvae with distilled water (dH₂O) and blot dry on tissue paper.

steps.title: Dissect larval tissues
steps.instruction: Place larvae in 1× PBS on a glass slide and dissect the desired internal tissues using fine forceps or dissecting needles.

steps.title: Fix tissues in PFA
steps.instruction: Transfer dissected tissues to a microcentrifuge tube containing freshly prepared 4% PFA, incubate at room temperature for 20 min, ensuring tissues are fully submerged and not adhering to tube walls.

steps.title: Wash after fixation
steps.instruction: Remove fixative and wash tissues with 200 µL 0.3% PBST on a rotator for 10 min at room temperature; repeat this wash three times.

steps.title: Permeabilize tissues
steps.instruction: Incubate tissues in 100 µL permeabilization buffer for 20 min at 4 °C on a rotator.

steps.title: Rinse with PBST
steps.instruction: Rinse tissues with 200 µL 0.3% PBST three times, 10 min each.

steps.title: Rinse with 2× SSC
steps.instruction: Rinse tissues with 200 µL 2× SSC twice, 10 min each.

steps.title: Prepare hybridization mixture
steps.instruction: For each 5–6 tissue sample, pipette ~30 µL of hybridization buffer (prepared above) into a 500 µL microcentrifuge tube and mix thoroughly with a 200 µL pipette.

steps.title: Hybridize probe
steps.instruction: Add the tissue to the hybridization mixture, seal the tube cap with parafilm, and incubate at 42 °C for 12–16 h.

steps.title: Wash with wash buffer
steps.instruction: Rinse tissues at 42 °C with pre‑warmed wash buffer three times, 5 min each.

steps.title: Wash with SSC series
steps.instruction: Rinse tissues at 42 °C with pre‑warmed 2× SSC then 1× SSC, each three times for 5 min.

steps.title: Final PBS washes
steps.instruction: Rinse tissues with 1× PBS at room temperature three times, 5 min each.

steps.title: Counterstain nuclei with DAPI
steps.instruction: Incubate tissues in 1 µg/mL DAPI solution for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Mount slides
steps.instruction: Mount tissues on glass slides using ProLong Gold antifade mountant, cover with a coverslip, seal edges with transparent nail polish, and store slides in the dark at –20 °C until imaging.

steps.title: Image fluorescence signals
steps.instruction: Examine slides on a fluorescence or confocal microscope using appropriate excitation and emission filters for Cy3 and DAPI; ensure fluorochrome spectra are well separated.
